key_insight: SMI turns medical concept codes into ontology-based semantic paths and combines them with frozen biomedical embeddings to better capture hierarchy, especially for rare and fine-grained concepts.
clinical_relevance: This could improve clinical prediction and recommendation systems by making representations of diagnoses, procedures, and medications more informative and robust across hospitals.
method: Build a Semantic ID for each concept using its coarse-to-fine path in a medical ontology.
Aggregate frozen biomedical LM embeddings across ontology levels to create hierarchy-aware concept representations.
Use either uniform weighting or validation-tuned level weights to emphasize more useful ontology levels.
evidence_signal: In experiments on MIMIC-IV and eICU, SMI improved mortality prediction, readmission prediction, drug recommendation, rare drug prediction, and robustness under cross-hospital shift.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the expert-defined ontology, and the weighted variant requires validation data to tune level weights.
paper_title: SMI: Ontology-Grounded Semantic IDs for Hierarchy-Aware Medical Concept Representation
